report.summary: Chunk 1 of artifacts.py: defines artifact families, path literal extraction, resolution candidates, and ArtifactEdge dataclass. Verifies docstring claims about tiers, invariants, and refusal to guess.
risks: extract_literals | low | MAX_LITERALS_PER_FILE=400 may silently truncate, losing edges; no warning or counting mechanism visible in this chunk. | Check if caller handles truncation or if a count is emitted elsewhere.

_candidates | medium | PurePosixPath(parent) of from_rel may produce '.' for root; then 'raw' is added again as './raw' duplication logic may be fragile. | Test with from_rel='file.txt' and raw='sub/file'.
artifact_node_id | low | Uses replace(chr(92), '/') but does not normalize forward slashes; path like 'a\b/c' becomes 'a/b/c' but 'a//b' stays. | Confirm normalization elsewhere.
literal_language | low | Falls back to suffix lookup; if suffix not in LITERAL_LANGUAGES returns None. For unknown suffixes, no literals extracted. | This is intentional per docstring.
LITERAL_RULES | low | Shell redirect pattern (?<![>])> may miss cases where > is preceded by a digit (e.g., '2>') or is part of '>>&'. | Check if shell rules cover common redirections.
extract_literals | low | line_of uses bisect on starts list built from newline positions; if text ends without newline, last line may be mis-indexed. | Test with file lacking trailing newline.
LITERAL_LANGUAGES | low | .C (capital C) mapped to 'cpp' not 'c'; may be C source. | Verify intent; C++ .C is common but ambiguous.
artifact_family | low | Only checks suffix; path like 'foo.root/' (directory) would match. | No defense against directories.
todos: Add counting of dropped literals due to MAX_LITERALS_PER_FILE.
Consider normalizing path separators consistently (e.g., pathlib).
Verify shell redirect pattern handles all common cases.
Review .C mapping to cpp vs c.

claims.text: The type layer describes **shapes declared in code** — what a function says it takes and returns. This layer describes **artefacts that move between programs** — which file a script reads, which it writes, and what schema that file actually carries.
claims.why: This chunk does not contain the type layer code; cannot verify claim about it.

claims.text: A path literal, however, is a path literal in LaTeX, C++, Python, Fortran, Verilog and a Makefile alike, which is why this layer generalises where the type layer cannot.
claims.why: LITERAL_RULES includes entries for all mentioned languages (latex, python, cpp, fortran, verilog, make).

claims.text: An edge alone says "this script touches that file". The interesting question is whether the **schema the code declares** and the **schema the file carries** agree.
claims.why: Schema comparison (compare_schema) is not in this chunk.

claims.text: So this module extracts artefact schemas as first-class data (``ArtifactSchema``) and offers ``compare_schema`` so a later lane can report the DISAGREEMENT
claims.why: ArtifactSchema and compare_schema are not defined in this chunk.

claims.text: tier 0  path literals -> artefact edges. No file is opened. Works for every language with a pattern below. This is the cheap universal layer.
claims.why: extract_literals reads text from string, no I/O; LITERAL_RULES covers many languages.

claims.text: tier 1  schema as DECLARED IN CODE (``TTree::Branch("voltage", …)``, ``read_csv(names=[…])``). Not implemented here yet; the hook is ``SCHEMA_FROM_CODE`` and it reports ``not_supported`` until it exists.
claims.why: SCHEMA_FROM_CODE not present in this chunk.

claims.text: tier 2  schema read FROM THE ARTEFACT. Implemented with stdlib only for CSV, JSON and NPY. ROOT/HDF5/Parquet need optional readers (``uproot``, ``h5py``, ``pyarrow``); absent, they report ``not_supported`` — never an empty schema
claims.why: Schema readers not implemented in this chunk.

claims.text: **Refuse to guess.** A literal that does not resolve to a file present in the file set is DROPPED and COUNTED, never bound to a near-match.
claims.why: Resolution logic not fully present; _candidates only generates candidates, no matching against file set.

claims.text: A literal matching more than one candidate is AMBIGUOUS and produces no edge.
claims.why: Ambiguity handling not implemented in this chunk.

claims.text: **Metadata only, never the payload.** A ``.root`` file is gigabytes; its branch list is kilobytes. Schema reads are bounded by ``MAX_SCHEMA_BYTES`` and stop at the header. This layer never ingests data.
claims.why: Schema reads not implemented; MAX_SCHEMA_BYTES defined but not used.

claims.text: **Reading is not executing.** No file here is imported, run, or evaluated. But parsing a hostile binary is still an attack surface, so every reader is bounded and failure is reported as ``unreadable``, never as an empty schema.
claims.why: Readers not implemented; UNREADABLE constant defined.

claims.text: **Artefacts are not code.** Artefact nodes get their own id namespace and never enter ``modules``, ``import_edges``, ``all_units`` or the symbol resolver
claims.why: artifact_node_id returns 'artifact:' prefix; is_artifact_node_id checks it; separate namespace evident.

claims.text: LaTeX omits the extension on \input and \includegraphics. Trying candidates is resolution, not guessing, PROVIDED that more than one hit is reported as ambiguous rather than silently taking the first.
claims.why: _candidates adds suffixes for 'includes' and 'figures' relations in latex; ambiguity handling not in this chunk but claim about trying candidates is implemented.

claims.text: A Makefile states producer and product outright — the only place in this table where direction is declared rather than inferred from a call name.
claims.why: _MAKE rule uses regex for target (writes) without call name inference.

claims.text: Deliberately by suffix, not by the ``LanguageSpec`` registry: this table includes formats that carry no code units at all (``.tex``, ``Makefile``) and therefore have no spec.
claims.why: LITERAL_LANGUAGES maps suffixes directly; .tex and .mk are present.

observations.what: MAX_LITERALS_PER_FILE is 400; extract_literals returns early if reached, but no warning or counting is emitted in this chunk.
_candidates uses PurePosixPath(parent) of from_rel; if from_rel has no directory part, parent is '.', leading to duplicate candidates.
artifact_node_id replaces backslashes but does not normalize forward slashes (e.g., '//' remains).
literal_language checks filename first, then suffix; but LITERAL_FILENAMES keys are lowercase, so 'Makefile' matches but 'MAKEFILE' may not.
Shell redirect pattern (?<![>])> may not match '2>' or '>>&'.
extract_literals uses bisect on starts list built from newline positions; if text does not end with newline, last line number may be off by one.
.C (capital C) is mapped to 'cpp' but could be C source.
artifact_family only checks suffix; path like 'foo.root/' (directory) would match.
